div.head: II Atr 9
div.ab: Hwilon stod, þæt man sceolde ðrywa tyman, ðær hit ærest befangen wære, ⁊ syððan fylgean teame, swa hwær swa man to cende. Ða geræddan witan, þæt hit betere wære, þæt man æure tymde, ðær hit ærest befangen wære, swa longe þæt man wiste, hwær hit ætstandan wolde, ðy læs ðe mon unmihtigne man to feor ⁊ to lange for his agenan swencte: swunce mare se, ðe þæt unriht gestreon on his handa stode, ⁊ læsse se ðe ðær ariht onspræce.

Aliquando fuit, quod ter aduocandum erat, ubi prius aliquid interciabatur, et deinceps eundum cum aduocante, quocumque aduocaret. Unde consuluerunt sapientes, quod melius erat, ut saltem aduocaretur ubi deprehendebatur, donec innotesceret, in quo stare uellet, ne forte impotens homo longius et diutius pro suo laboraret, et ut uexetur magis qui iniuste conquisitum habet in manibus, et minus qui iuste prosequitur.

[Be teamum.] Hwilon stod þæt man sceolde ðrywa tyman ðær hit ærest befangen wære, ⁊ syððan fylgean teame, swa hwær swa man to cende. Ða geræddan witan, þæt hit betere wære, þæt man æure tymde ðær hit ærest befangen wære, swa longe þæt man wiste hwær hit ætstandan wolde, ðy læs ðe mon unmihtigne man to feor ⁊ to lange for his agenan swencte. Swunce mare se ðe þæt unriht gestreon on his handa stode ⁊ læsse se ðe ðær ariht onspræce.

(Von Gewährzügen. Ld) Vormals [zwar] galt, dass [die Gewähr nur die] drei [ersten] Male da, wo es zuerst im Anefang gefasst war, gezogen zu werden brauchte, fernerhin aber [Kläger] dem Gewährzuge folgen [musste], an welchen Ort auch immer der [ziehende] Mann hin erklärte. Da beschlossen die Witan, dass es besser wäre, dass allemal dort, wo es zuerst im Anefang gefasst war, [der Gewährsmann] herbeigezogen würde, so oft, bis sich aufkläre, wo es [das zur Gewährziehen] stillstehen wird: damit ein unvermögender Mann [als Kläger im Anefang] nicht zu weit fort und zu lange wegen [Wiedererlangung] seines Eigenthums belästigt werde. Die Mühe [der Reise] trage vielmehr, wem unrechtmässiger Erwerb in seiner Hand sich befunden, und weniger der, welcher da rechtmässig geklagt hat.

(Of vouching to warranty. Ld) Formerly it was the rule that [the warrantor] had to be vouched three times at the place where it was first attached, and after that [the claimant had to] follow the vouching wherever the [vouching] man declared it. Then the witan decided that it would be better for [the warrantor] always to be vouched at the place where it was first attached, until it became clear where it [the vouching] would come to a stop: so that a man without means [suing by attachment] would not be put to trouble too far and too long for [the recovery of] his own property. Rather let him bear the trouble [of travelling] in whose hands the unlawful acquisition was found, and less he who made a lawful claim there.

Formerly it was the rule that vouching to warranty for the first three times should take place where the goods were first attached, and afterwards the process should be transferred to the locality indicated (by the evidence of the third person). Then the authorities decided that it would be better for the vouching to warranty always to take place where the property was first attached, until it should appear where the process would end, lest a man of small means should be burdened by long and distant journeys in order to recover his property. The burden should rather be borne by him who has in his possession property to which he is not entitled, than by him who is putting forward a just claim to it.

Mit demselben Beweggrund und in denselben Worten wird abgeschafftem Gesetz (s. d. Gl 22) das nunmehrige entgegengestellt Forf 3.—Diese Begrenzung der Reisemühe des Klägers und späterhin des Gewährziehens auf nur drei Male (s. Gl Anefang 25)—eine Entwicklung im Ggs. zu I Ew 1, 1 (Rauch Spurfolge 9f.)—hält Steenstrup (Danelag 372) für Nordisch beeinflusst, gibt aber zu, dass beides auch anderswo vorkommt

With the same motive and in the same words, Forf 3 sets the present law against the abolished one (see that word in Gl 22). — This limitation of the claimant’s trouble of travelling, and later of vouching to warranty, to only three times (see Gl Anefang 25) — a development in contrast to I Ew 1, 1 (Rauch Spurfolge 9f.) — Steenstrup (Danelag 372) considers to be due to Norse influence, though he admits that both occur elsewhere too
Ellipse des Subjekts; dass hier ein anderes eintritt, verkennen frühere Übersetzer
Ellipsis of the subject; earlier translators fail to recognize that a different one comes in here

willan hier futurisch; Präteritum weil von geræddan abhängig. Der Gewährzug endet, sobald der letzte Bezogene entweder als Dieb ertappt wird oder mit seinem Ureigeneide durchdringt, der den Anefang (s. d. Gl 27) als falsche Klage (d. 7d) erweist

willan here has future sense; preterite because dependent on geræddan. Vouching to warranty ends as soon as the last person vouched is either caught as a thief or prevails with his oath of original ownership, which proves the attachment (see that word in Gl 27) to be a false accusation (that word 7d)
swencan ist transitiv, swincan intr.; s. Wb. Das Praet. hängt von geræddan ab.—Vgl. Gl Reise 1
swencan is transitive, swincan intr.; see Wb. The pret. depends on geræddan. — Cf. Gl Reise 1
i.e. then and not till then.
